thread.title: Apple ( AAPL ) took a huge hit on Friday, after the fiscal Q

author: J. M. Manness
title: Apple ( AAPL ) took a huge hit on Friday, after the fiscal Q
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) took a huge hit on Friday, after the fiscal Q1 earnings announcement. Shares closed down 4.3% to $160.50, the lowest levels since October.
The question is, was this drop warranted? Are the details of the earnings release so negative that Apple should move ahead into a major correction?
I believe not. I believe that Apple has presented a very strong quarter with plenty to grow on, and that negativity comes from a poor analysis of the data that ignores a very crucial point .
It is my experience that while Apple has its fans, it also has a legion of naysayers trying to put a negative spin on any news, always predicting doom. (Look at all the negative reaction to the introduction of the original iPhone, for example.)
The savvy investor needs to see through the smoke of these detractors, to find the core value.
The retraction seems to be driven by two lines of thought here.
The first focuses on the 1% drop in iPhone sales. The second focuses on March quarter projections of $60-62 billion revenue, below market analysts’ estimates. On the second point, Reuters reported : 
Analysts at Longbow Research said the revenue guidance implied a low 50 million iPhone shipment forecast against a consensus of 58.5 million. 
I will address the iPhone projections in a separate post; here I will address the “poor results in comparison to last year” meme. 
First some numbers Apple announced revenue of $88.3 billion, up 13% from the year-ago quarter, and EPS of $3.89, up 16%. Both beat consensus estimates which, according to Thomson Reuters, were $3.86 EPS on $87.28 billion revenue.
So why the fuss? It comes down to the numbers – too many were below last year’s.
